project.name: Generic Pipeline and Workflow Components Framework

referenceConsumer.role: Reference consumer for target-specific integration design and end-to-end acceptance

purpose: Establish Prefect as GPWCF's adopted external workflow runtime and define the target-specific integration architecture, responsibility boundaries, mapping of the reference consumer's thirteen specified stages, implementation sequence, and traceable acceptance plan. This document authorizes integration design and implementation; it does not claim that full GPWCF-to-Prefect conformance has already been implemented or verified.

decisionRecord.title: Adopt Prefect 3 as the External Workflow Runtime
decisionRecord.decision: Adopt Prefect 3 as the selected external workflow runtime for GPWCF. Use Prefect-native Flows/Subflows and Tasks as execution constructs while preserving GPWCF-owned component contracts, semantic composition, typed outcomes, identity domains, artifact custody, and specialized relationship rules.
decisionRecord.authority: User-approved technology selection following the candidate assessment and reference-consumer PoC evidence. This decision supersedes the prior open comparative candidate-selection position for the primary GPWCF integration target.

selectedBaseline.executionProfile: Native local process execution; local Prefect API/server profile selected for initial integration qualification
selectedBaseline.pinningRule: The exact version is the initial integration baseline. A complete reproducible lock of all direct/transitive dependencies and selected extras is a required implementation deliverable; do not silently float to latest.
selectedBaseline.license: Apache-2.0; verify exact installed distribution metadata and transitive dependency licenses in the dependency manifest before distribution.

rationale: Prefect is Python-native and permits GPWCF callable implementations and workflow definitions to execute within the same managed CPython environment without a mandatory cross-language worker boundary.
The local Prefect 3.9.2 reference-consumer report records successful native Windows x64 execution under the managed CPython 3.15.1 runtime.

The recorded ten-run fixture matrix covered Stage invocation, artifact handoff, independent prerequisite branches, provider fan-out/fan-in, and conditional publication; 32 Request Envelopes and 32 Result Envelopes passed Draft 2020-12 validation.
Prefect's Flow/Subflow and Task execution model is a credible native realization for the adopted Pipeline Root -> Stage Parent Workflow -> Step Subworkflow -> executable-node hierarchy.

The adoption decision is based on combined architectural fit and local evidence. Remaining full-hierarchy, lifecycle, and operational acceptance work is converted into explicit implementation gates rather than reopening candidate comparison.

recordedEvidence: Prefect 3.9.2 installed and version-verified in an isolated environment based on managed CPython 3.15.1.
Native Windows execution and temporary loopback API server startup succeeded.
Ten final flat/hierarchical fixture scenario runs passed.
All 32 Request Envelopes and 32 Result Envelopes passed Draft 2020-12 validation with format checking.
Stage 5/6 provider invocations overlapped in the tested task-level dynamic fan-out topology.
Conditional publication behavior was verified: Stage 13 ran for Publishable and did not run for ValidationFailed.
explicitLimits: The previous PoC used Stage-opaque fixture invocation and is not proof of real GPWCF Stage/Step/SPU integration.

A repeated-child-flow fan-out experiment returned both child results but observed serialized execution in that tested local topology; the accepted fixture topology used task-level fan-out for complete Stage invocations. Retest this observation; do not generalize it to every Prefect child-flow deployment pattern.
Pipeline Root multi-Stage integration, Step-as-independent-Subflow, SPU Functional Binding, and Supporting Unit binding at all permitted scopes were not established by the prior PoC.
Cancellation/timeout settlement, retry/replay idempotency, process-tree termination, failure isolation, restart/recovery, persistence durability, and production operational profile remain unverified.
evidenceBaseline.decisionInterpretation: The evidence is sufficient to select Prefect as the target technology. It is not evidence that the integration acceptance gates below have passed.

supersedes: The no-final-candidate-selected status in 01.04_Build_vs_Adopt_vs_Adapt_Decisions.json is superseded for the primary workflow-runtime selection by this accepted decision.
The documentary candidate shortlist remains historical evidence and is not an active requirement to keep comparing Prefect with Dagu, Temporal, or other candidates.
The Target Hierarchical Integration Model v1.1.0 and its Functional Binding/Hierarchical Nesting objectives remain normative and are not superseded.

positive: Implementation can target one concrete runtime and its native execution primitives.
Python-native integration avoids a mandatory separate worker language/runtime for the initial local deployment.
Existing Prefect fixture PoC artifacts can be reused as regression evidence.
tradeoffs: GPWCF must implement and maintain Prefect-specific integration code and pin a compatible dependency set.
Prefect-native run states and identifiers cannot replace GPWCF domain results or identity types.
The local Prefect service/persistence profile and durability characteristics must be selected explicitly.
Prefect topology and concurrency behavior must be proven for the exact chosen execution mode; the prior repeated-child-flow fan-out observation is a known design risk.

governingPrinciples.name: External Runtime Owns Execution
governingPrinciples.rule: Prefect owns native workflow definition/execution, scheduling, dispatch, dependency evaluation, and native operational state. GPWCF does not implement a parallel scheduler, workflow engine, or graph executor.

governingPrinciples.name: GPWCF Owns Semantics
governingPrinciples.rule: GPWCF remains authoritative for Stage/Step/SPU/Supporting Unit identities, callable contracts, composition meaning, permitted transitions, typed results, Error/Failure semantics, lifecycle obligations, and artifact contracts.

governingPrinciples.name: Stage Boundary Preservation
governingPrinciples.rule: Every GPWCF Stage is exposed as a Prefect Parent Flow invocation boundary. Every GPWCF Step is represented by a native nested Flow/Subflow boundary or verified equivalent, invoked through the public Step contract.

governingPrinciples.name: Step Boundary Cannot Be Bypassed
governingPrinciples.rule: A Stage Flow invokes Step Subflows through Step[TInput,TOutput].execute and consumes StepExecutionResult. It must not call Step-owned SPU or Supporting Unit tasks directly.

governingPrinciples.name: Functional Binding Is Explicit
governingPrinciples.rule: Every executable GPWCF responsibility is mapped through a versioned binding declaration to a native Prefect Flow/Task execution element and its specialized callable contract. No universal plugin protocol or generic component interface is implied.

governingPrinciples.name: Relationship Mechanism Is Semantic
governingPrinciples.rule: Use native Flow invocation, Task dependency, containment/composition, reference passing, event/observation mechanisms, or explicit specialized association only when that mechanism preserves the applicable contract semantics. Association is not a universal requirement.

governingPrinciples.name: Runtime IDs Are Not Domain IDs
governingPrinciples.rule: Prefect Flow Run and Task Run IDs are operational correlation identifiers. They never replace GPWCF Pipeline, Stage, Step, SPU, Supporting Unit, association, invocation, attempt, or artifact identities.

governingPrinciples.name: Runtime State Is Not Domain Outcome
governingPrinciples.rule: Prefect State/StateType and orchestration exceptions are execution evidence. They do not replace SPUExecutionResult, StepExecutionResult, Stage Flow Result, Stage outputs, ErrorResult, ErrorHandlerResult, or domain support decisions.

governingPrinciples.name: Artifact References Across Boundaries
governingPrinciples.rule: Use small serializable control envelopes and immutable artifact references at Flow/Task boundaries. Large, binary, or semantically governed artifacts remain in the consumer-owned artifact store with sidecar envelopes and digests.

governingPrinciples.name: No In-Place Mutation
governingPrinciples.rule: Published artifacts and accepted results remain immutable. Retries and corrections create new attempt/run/artifact identities; downstream consumers validate exact versions and digests.

governingPrinciples.name: No Implied Retry Safety
governingPrinciples.rule: Retry is enabled only for operations whose specialized contract and idempotency/reconciliation strategy explicitly permit replay. Prefect retry configuration alone does not establish safe retry.

governingPrinciples.name: Evidence Before Conformance Claims
governingPrinciples.rule: Documented Prefect capability, prior fixture evidence, implemented adapter behavior, and accepted GPWCF conformance are separate evidence levels.

governingPrinciples.name: Optional Infrastructure Stays Optional
governingPrinciples.rule: No mandatory Docker, Kubernetes, Redis, PostgreSQL, cloud service, LLM provider, external message broker, universal plugin manager, or global runtime registry is introduced for the initial local profile.

governingPrinciples.name: Consumer Owns Business Workflow
governingPrinciples.rule: The Generator owns its actual stage specialization, artifact semantics, tooling choices, and business decisions. GPWCF supplies reusable contracts; Prefect executes the resulting native hierarchy.

goals: Adopt Prefect 3 as the single selected external workflow runtime for GPWCF's initial target-specific integration.
Realize Pipeline Root -> multiple Stage Parent Flows -> Step Subflows -> SPU/Supporting Unit executable elements.
Preserve GPWCF callable contracts, component identities, typed outcomes, exception distinctions, context, artifact custody, lifecycle, and provenance.
Map the complete PayloadDescriptionGenerator Stage 1-13 dependency graph and workload multiplicities into Prefect-native execution.
Provide a Windows x64 / CPython 3.15.1 local execution and persistence profile with reproducible dependency closure.
Deliver an end-to-end vertical integration with traceable acceptance evidence.
nonGoals: Replacing Prefect with a GPWCF-owned scheduler, workflow engine, universal graph executor, or state machine.
Creating a universal adapter across multiple workflow products.
Creating a universal Plugin Manager, Plugin Registry, or dynamic loader.
Treating every Stage Model objective or execution_steps entry as a GPWCF Step or SPU without contract-based decomposition.
Forcing every Supporting Unit to be a Prefect Task or requiring Association for every functional binding.
Moving Generator domain artifacts, large payloads, or semantic result ownership into Prefect's orchestration database.
Changing the Generator's Stage specifications, schemas, artifact contracts, or business semantics as a side effect of integration.
Making Docker/Kubernetes, distributed workers, cloud hosting, LLMs, Redis, or PostgreSQL mandatory for the first local profile.

hierarchy.boundary: One root invocation coordinates the required Stage Parent Flow runs, shared invocation-wide prerequisites, branch dependencies, final result, and pipeline-level operational evidence.
mustPreserve: Pipeline run identity distinct from Prefect root Flow Run ID
Multiple independently identifiable Stage invocations
Stage-specific inputs, outputs, Flow Results, exceptions, and artifacts
Root-level context, cancellation request, completion/settlement, and final pipeline result

hierarchy.boundary: The Stage Flow is the external invocation realization of the GPWCF Stage facade. Its internal graph follows Stage-specific composition semantics.
mustPreserve: Stage identity and public callable contract
Stage-owned Step membership and transition semantics
StepExecutionResult collection and invocation-exception records
Stage-specific Flow Result and Stage outputs
Stage error occurrences and lifecycle facts

hierarchy.boundary: The Step Subflow is independently identifiable and invoked through the public Step.execute contract; it owns its internal composition.
mustPreserve: Step instance and invocation identity
Typed TInput and TOutput
StepExecutionResult[TOutput] distinct from Prefect State
Step Composition flow result and internal evidence
Internal SPU/Supporting Unit selection, association, lifecycle and custody

hierarchy.prefectRepresentation: Prefect Task or other native executable element inside the owning Step Flow
hierarchy.boundary: A Task binds the actual specialized SPU callable; it does not become the Step or own Step-level aggregation.
mustPreserve: SPU-specific input/output types
SPUExecutionResult[TOutput]
SPU identity and invocation/attempt provenance
SPUError occurrences distinct from thrown exceptions

hierarchy.prefectRepresentation: Native Task/Flow/activity/extension selected for the specialized contract and scope
hierarchy.boundary: Executable Supporting Unit responsibilities are bound at a contract-permitted scope; non-executable semantic models are not converted into runtime nodes.
mustPreserve: Pattern-specific callable/event/result semantics
Independent Supporting Unit identity
Permitted scope and applicable relationship constraints
Specialized lifecycle and evidence custody

logicalComponents.name: Root Integration Boundary
logicalComponents.responsibility: Translate one consumer pipeline invocation into a Prefect Root Flow invocation; pass invocation context; include/invoke multiple Stage Flows; correlate their run identities and collect the consumer-defined pipeline result.

logicalComponents.name: Stage Flow Binding
logicalComponents.responsibility: Bind a concrete Stage facade and Stage specialization to a Prefect Flow while preserving its public input/output, Stage Flow Result, flow transitions, errors, and artifacts.

logicalComponents.name: Step Subflow Binding
logicalComponents.responsibility: Bind each concrete Step public execute contract to a nested Prefect Flow invocation and preserve StepExecutionResult, exceptions, identity, and lifecycle settlement.

logicalComponents.name: Executable Functional Binding
logicalComponents.responsibility: Bind SPU and executable Supporting Unit callables to Prefect Tasks or other native execution elements within the correct owner boundary.

logicalComponents.name: Functional Binding Manifest
logicalComponents.responsibility: Versioned declarations of GPWCF role/component/function identity, specialized contract version, native Prefect definition/callable, scope, input/output/result contract, and conformance evidence. This is an explicit integration artifact, not a dynamic plugin registry.

logicalComponents.name: Invocation and Context Envelope
logicalComponents.responsibility: Carry correlation identities, parent/child invocation context, request selectors, artifact references, contract versions, and cancellation/deadline context across native boundaries without erasing specialized inputs.

logicalComponents.name: Typed Result and Failure Mapper
logicalComponents.responsibility: Map native call return, exception, and operational state into GPWCF-owned typed results and separately recorded invocation exceptions; never coerce one category into another.

logicalComponents.name: Artifact Reference and Custody Bridge
logicalComponents.responsibility: Pass immutable artifact references and sidecar envelope identities; verify schema/version/digest and custody transitions; avoid transporting large artifacts as Prefect parameters/results.

logicalComponents.name: Lifecycle and Settlement Mapper
logicalComponents.responsibility: Translate GPWCF admission, quiescence, retention/reuse, terminal retirement, cancellation, timeout, recovery, and settlement obligations to Prefect operations where compatible, and report unsupported/indeterminate outcomes explicitly.

logicalComponents.name: Execution Evidence Correlator
logicalComponents.responsibility: Correlate Prefect Flow/Task run IDs, parent/child run links, logs and states with GPWCF domain identities and immutable result/artifact evidence.

gpwcf: Stage, Step, SPU and Supporting Unit semantic identities and public callable contracts.
Stage and Step composition membership, flow semantics, dependencies, transition conditions, and decision meanings.
SPUExecutionResult, StepExecutionResult, Stage Flow Result, ErrorResult, ErrorHandlerResult and other specialized result meanings.
Error Model and specialized Error/Failure/Occurrence contracts.
Association and lifecycle invariants and pattern-specific specializations.
Artifact schemas, sidecar envelopes, identity domains, canonicalization, immutability and custody.
prefect: Native Flow, Subflow, Task and supported deployment/work-pool/worker definitions.
Native scheduling, dispatch, dependency execution, concurrency primitives, retries/timeouts where selected, and operational state.
Native Flow Run and Task Run identity and execution history.
Native runtime execution, supported cancellation operations, and local service/worker lifecycle.
integrationBoundary: Versioned functional binding and hierarchy mapping.
Serialization-safe boundary envelopes and correlation mapping.
Typed result, exception, artifact-reference, event and lifecycle translation.
Target-specific conformance verification and explicit weaker/unsupported behavior reporting.
referenceConsumer: Concrete Stage and Step specialization, SPU/Supporting Unit implementation and selection.
Generator business/artifact semantics, stage-specific topology, tooling and profile decisions.
Workspace, compiler, provider, registry, schema and artifact-store configuration.
Consumer-specific retry, concurrency, output and operational policies where not fixed by GPWCF contracts.

prohibitedShortcuts: Stage Flow directly invokes an SPU Task belonging to a Step, bypassing the Step Subflow.
Prefect Completed/Failed/Cancelled state is substituted for a GPWCF domain result.
A thrown Python exception is automatically converted into SPUError or StageError.
Prefect run IDs replace GPWCF component/invocation identities.
A Prefect result backend is treated as the authoritative Generator artifact store without explicit artifact contract approval.
A generic adapter erases the specialized signatures or result types of SPUs and Supporting Units.
A Root Association construct or global association registry is added solely to connect multiple Stage Flows.
A retry is enabled for publication, output, or other side-effecting work without idempotency and reconciliation proof.
A timeout or cancelled state is treated as proof that an underlying native child process has terminated.

stageMapping.name: Build Context Discovery
stageMapping.flowRole: Invocation/environment-wide Stage Parent Flow; execute once per Generator invocation/environment inventory scope, not once per payload type.
stageMapping.objectiveGroupRule: These are Stage Model objectives, not automatically GPWCF Steps. Derive concrete Step Subflows from the approved Stage specialization and Step contracts.
prefectExecutionNotes: Root Flow establishes invocation identity and invokes STG-01 before consumers requiring its inventory.
Verify the pre-provisioned isolated Python runtime, packages, CastXML/pygccxml resources, schemas, registries and native tools without installing/downloading.
Compiler/toolchain candidates remain candidates; STG-01 does not select a compiler or resolve Compilation Contexts.

stageMapping.name: Compilation Context Resolution
stageMapping.flowRole: Invocation-wide Stage Parent Flow consuming immutable STG-01 inventory; resolve all relevant Compilation Contexts and TU associations.
prefectExecutionNotes: Requires the exact immutable STG-01 inventory and fingerprint.
Preserve per-TU invocation evidence, freshness, conflicts, unknowns and context equivalence; do not collapse contexts by convenience.
STG-02 may overlap STG-03 after root invocation context and request are established, because STG-03 type capture does not require resolved C++ compilation contexts.

stageMapping.name: Payload Type Input
stageMapping.flowRole: Per requested payload-type branch Stage Parent Flow; may execute concurrently with STG-02 after root invocation establishment.
prefectExecutionNotes: Preserve the requested C++ type designator and input envelope; do not infer compilation context from the type input.
Keep request identity distinct from Pipeline Run and Prefect Flow Run identities.
STG-04 is admitted only after its required STG-01, STG-02 and STG-03 inputs are available.

stageMapping.name: Type Resolution
stageMapping.flowRole: Per payload-type request Stage Parent Flow; may aggregate multiple context-bound candidate/declaration bindings.
prefectExecutionNotes: Search all authorized bounded roots and preserve all candidates and applicable contexts.
No first-match precedence or hidden fallback is permitted; ambiguity and unresolved results remain explicit.
Stage 5/6 fan-out is derived from the exact resolved binding set.

stageMapping.name: AST Extraction
stageMapping.flowRole: Per provider/binding executable Stage invocation; one logical Stage boundary per complete Stage 5 invocation.
prefectExecutionNotes: Bind every provider invocation to the exact resolved binding and Compilation Context.
Preserve provider-native observations, source/TU/context lineage and diagnostics; Stage 7 owns canonical declaration identity.
Stage 5 and Stage 6 are eligible for parallel execution for the same binding only when their exact context binding is equal.

stageMapping.name: XML Generation
stageMapping.flowRole: Per provider/binding executable Stage invocation; paired provider branch alongside STG-05 when allowed by the exact context.
prefectExecutionNotes: Same exact Compilation Context and resolved binding as paired Stage 5 branch are mandatory for comparability.
Preserve XML provider observations and lineage independently; do not treat Stage 5/6 outputs as canonical declarations.
The prior PoC's successful task-level dynamic fan-out is regression evidence only; actual Prefect concurrency and child-flow behavior must be proven for selected execution mode.

stageMapping.name: Declaration Analysis
stageMapping.flowRole: Per payload-type request Stage Parent Flow performing provider reconciliation and declaration graph construction after Stage 4/5/6 dependencies settle.
prefectExecutionNotes: Native Prefect dependencies provide fan-in only after required Stage 5/6 branches complete or produce an explicitly permitted missing-provider outcome.
Stage 7 owns DeclarationIds, CanonicalCppTypeKeys, ResolvedTypeIds and provider-neutral graph reconciliation.
Provider absence is tolerated only under an explicit approved capability/coverage rule; missing observations are not silently synthesized.

stageMapping.name: Dependency Resolution
stageMapping.flowRole: Per payload-type request Stage Parent Flow consuming authoritative Stage 7 declaration/type graph.
prefectExecutionNotes: Preserve cycles and strongly connected components as domain graph facts; do not convert cycles into orchestration cycles unless the stage contract explicitly requires repeated execution.
The resolved graph and closure boundaries are immutable handoff artifacts for downstream stages.

stageMapping.name: Logical Description
stageMapping.flowRole: Per payload-type request Stage Parent Flow consuming Stage 7/8 authoritative structures and publishing the Logical Description.
prefectExecutionNotes: Stage 9 owns stable logical identities and logical relationships; it must not replace declaration or provider identities.
Validate/canonicalize/publish the exact LD contract and sidecar envelope; downstream stages consume immutable references.

stageMapping.name: Physical Layout Extraction
stageMapping.flowRole: Context-bound Stage invocations; produce one PLD per resolved type and exact Compilation Context.
prefectExecutionNotes: Each PLD is bound to one exact resolved type/context pair; do not aggregate incompatible contexts into one PLD.
Keep native physical facts, evidence, layout-control applications and support/coverage records under Stage 10 ownership.
The extraction adapter acquires provider evidence; Stage 10 composition performs authoritative normalization/reconciliation and publication.

stageMapping.name: Description Composition
stageMapping.flowRole: Representation-qualified Stage invocations; produce separate SAM artifacts for distinct selected representation/profile versions.
prefectExecutionNotes: Each SAM is bound to exact LD/PLD/context and representation profile/rule-set identity/version/fingerprint.
Distinct representation profiles produce distinct SAM artifacts; no global type-level support claim is inferred.
Named Pipe is not a representation profile; it may be a transport for a message payload only.

stageMapping.name: Validation
stageMapping.flowRole: Per exact LD × applicable PLD/context × SAM representation profile/version combination; Stage Parent Flow with dependent validation objectives and nine semantic validation gates.
prefectExecutionNotes: Model the nine gates and twelve objective groups as a Stage-specific graph; do not assume every gate is parallelizable or that objective count equals Step count.
Preserve exact validation-combination identity and all pinned schema, registry, policy, profile and rule-set fingerprints.
Unknown, unavailable, conflicting, unresolved, or extracted-but-unverified facts must not be promoted to ValidatedSupported.
Stage 12 owns the Validation Report and representation-scoped support decision; Prefect state does not substitute for either.

stageMapping.name: Output Generation
stageMapping.flowRole: Conditional final Stage Parent Flow invoked only when exact Stage 12 result permits publication; ValidationFailed yields diagnostics only.
prefectExecutionNotes: Invoke STG-13 only for a permitted Stage 12 support outcome under the Stage 13 contract.
Verify every artifact's exact identity and digest before assembly; preserve validated content byte-for-byte.
Use the approved canonical serializer and exact integer-token preservation; publication is immutable and versioned.
ValidationFailed must not produce a package or Output Manifest; emit only the separate non-consumable diagnostic record.

objectiveAndStepDecomposition.rule: A Stage Model objective is a documented responsibility grouping. An execution_steps entry is a documented processing action. Neither is automatically a GPWCF Step, SPU, or Prefect Task. The concrete Stage specialization must first identify GPWCF Step instances and their public Step[TInput,TOutput].execute contracts. Each Step Subflow then binds that public contract; only the Step's own approved composition decomposition binds SPUs and executable Supporting Units to Tasks.
objectiveAndStepDecomposition.acceptance: No Stage implementation is accepted while it uses objective IDs or execution_steps IDs as surrogate Step/SPU identities without an approved contract-based mapping.

supportingUnitBinding.principle: Supporting Unit identity is independent of its native Prefect executable representation and of the scope to which it is functionally bound. A reusable Supporting Unit contract may be bound at a scope only when that specialized contract permits it.

permittedScopes.prefectBinding: Task or local executable callable inside the SPU execution boundary
permittedScopes.rule: Only when the specialized Supporting Unit contract permits SPU-level binding.

permittedScopes.prefectBinding: Task or nested executable element inside the owning Step Subflow
permittedScopes.rule: Step Composition retains selection, invocation, result custody and applicable association/lifecycle authority.

permittedScopes.prefectBinding: Task or Flow activity inside the Stage Flow
permittedScopes.rule: Must be Stage-owned/Stage-permitted; cannot bypass a Step-owned component boundary.

permittedScopes.prefectBinding: Task or Flow activity inside the Root Flow
permittedScopes.rule: Must be explicitly pipeline-root permitted; must not centralize Step-owned internal components.

patterns.rule: Defines Error Type Definitions, Error Occurrences and ErrorResult meaning/aggregation. It is not an executable Prefect Task.

patterns.representation: Prefect Task or callable bound within its owning Step Subflow
patterns.rule: Executes handling operations under specialized input/result, publication, reservation, identity and recovery contracts. It is not interchangeable with Error Modeling.
Preserve validator-specific outcomes, evidence, timing and gating semantics.

patterns.representation: Task, event/callback integration or other supported native mechanism
patterns.rule: Preserve zero/one/many observation semantics, subscriptions/events, destination and lifecycle; observation is not automatically StepExecutionResult content.

invariants: Do not introduce a generic SupportingUnit base class or universal runtime component type solely for Prefect.
Do not require all Supporting Unit patterns at all scopes.
Keep instance identity, invocation/activity identity, association identity, target identity and Prefect run identity distinct.
Apply association only when the selected specialized contract requires it; native task dependency or containment is not a substitute for a required specialized association.
Step Composition remains authoritative for Step-internal selection, association, flow and lifecycle decisions.

identityDomains.rule: Store as correlated pair; GPWCF identity remains authoritative.

identityDomains.prefectEvidence: Stage Flow definition identity + Stage Flow Run ID
identityDomains.rule: A reusable Stage definition and each invocation are distinct.
Preserve independent Step boundary and parent Stage correlation.

identityDomains.prefectEvidence: Task definition/run ID and retry/attempt evidence
identityDomains.rule: One SPU invocation/result remains distinguishable from every attempt and native Task Run.

identityDomains.prefectEvidence: Native Task/Flow run or event correlation
identityDomains.rule: Do not overload component identity with activity identity.

identityDomains.prefectEvidence: Artifact reference stored in parameters/returns/log metadata
identityDomains.rule: Prefect run ID is provenance metadata, not artifact identity.

envelopeRequirements: GPWCF pipeline run identity and optional consumer request/type identity.
Stage, Step, SPU and Supporting Unit identities applicable to the invocation.
Invocation identity, attempt identity, parent invocation identity and correlation identity.
Prefect Flow Run ID / Task Run ID when known, stored as operational correlation only.
Specialized contract/schema versions and binding-manifest identity/version.
Compilation Context ID/fingerprint and other consumer-specific context references.
Immutable artifact IDs, locations, schema/contract IDs, versions, digests and custody state.
Deadline/cancellation context only where the public GPWCF contract supports it; never pass process-local handles as serialized context.

resultMapping.rule: Normal return remains the structured SPU result. A Task return wrapper may carry it only if serialization/custody is proven.
The Step Subflow returns the exact Step result contract; it is not replaced by Task state.
Stage Composition assembles the domain Flow Result from Step results, exceptions, transitions and StageError occurrences.
Keep Completed/Failed/Cancelled states separate from domain outcomes.

resultMapping.target: Invocation exception record / specialized exception path
resultMapping.rule: Do not synthesize SPUError/StageError or a successful structured result automatically.
Prefect branch/conditional execution uses the exact support-decision artifact; orchestration state is not the decision.

serializationPolicy.allowed: Small JSON-serializable invocation envelopes, typed metadata, stable scalar values, and immutable artifact references.
serializationPolicy.disallowedByDefault: Large AST/XML payloads, large compiler outputs, binary payloads, mutable object graphs, open file handles, subprocess handles, and live runtime object references.
serializationPolicy.artifactStoreOwner: SMRB.PayloadDescriptionGenerator / consuming application under the Artifact Envelope and Description Package contracts.
serializationPolicy.validation: Schema/version/digest validation occurs at the receiving boundary before use.

concurrency.owner: Prefect performs actual scheduling/concurrency; GPWCF and the concrete Stage specialization define which work is allowed to overlap and what must join.
initialExpectedPatterns: STG-02 and STG-03 may overlap after invocation establishment.
STG-05 and STG-06 may overlap for the same exact resolved binding and Compilation Context.
Multiple eligible Stage 5/6 provider invocations may fan out dynamically when their contracts permit.
STG-07 joins required Stage 5/6 observation branches before cross-provider reconciliation.
STG-10 invocations may fan out by exact resolved type × Compilation Context pair.
STG-11 invocations may fan out by distinct applicable representation profile/rule-set combination.
STG-12 validation work is parallelized only where its objective/gate dependency graph proves independence.
STG-13 publication remains gated by the exact Stage 12 support decision.
constraints: Concurrency limits are configuration, not hidden constants.
Concurrent completion must not make result aggregation nondeterministic where the contract requires deterministic ordering.
The exact Prefect task runner and concurrency mechanism are selected only after a focused implementation experiment; the previous child-flow fan-out observation must be included.

retries.rule: No global retry policy. Retry is declared per Step/SPU/Supporting Unit operation only after idempotency, immutable input/output, attempt identity, side-effect boundaries and recovery semantics are defined.
retries.initialDefault: No automatic retry for side-effecting publication or custody-transfer operations. Retry disabled unless explicit binding/contract policy permits it.
requirements: Distinguish invocation identity from attempt identity.
Preserve outputs/evidence produced before a later failure under the specialized recovery contract.
Use exact immutable inputs and version pins for replay.
Reconcile uncertain publication/custody before any retry that could duplicate an accepted operation.

cancellationAndTimeout.rule: Prefect cancellation/timeout is a runtime request or state transition, not proof of GPWCF lifecycle settlement or native process termination.
requirements: Define cancellation propagation Root -> Stage -> Step -> executable work.
Determine whether selected local execution mode can terminate or only cancel orchestration of a running Python/subprocess operation.
Track child process/process-tree handles only in the owning execution adapter and reconcile their termination separately.
Preserve accepted artifacts/results and recovery ownership after cancellation.
Report confirmed, failed, or indeterminate settlement distinctly.
Do not release/reuse a Step or Supporting Unit until its own lifecycle contract confirms the required disposition.

failureIsolationAndRecovery: A failed independent branch blocks only dependent branches where the Stage specification permits isolation.
A Prefect Failed state must be paired with the exact GPWCF exception/result/evidence record.
Partial diagnostics are published only when their schema, identity and consumption safety are valid.
Unresolved output custody or terminal retirement retains a named recovery owner and access path.
Root failure aggregation follows the consumer pipeline contract; it is not inferred from the count of failed Prefect runs.

stateAndPersistence.distinction: Prefect run state/history is operational execution history; Generator artifacts and GPWCF typed outcomes are separate authoritative data.
stateAndPersistence.localProfile: Use the selected local Prefect API/server and SQLite persistence profile for the first durable local integration profile, after restart/durability verification.
stateAndPersistence.testProfile: An ephemeral loopback API profile may be used for isolated unit/contract tests only where its non-durable behavior is explicit.
stateAndPersistence.productionExpansion: PostgreSQL/Redis or distributed worker infrastructure is considered only for a separately approved multi-worker/multi-server deployment profile; it is not a prerequisite for the initial local profile.
acceptance: Document data directory and database ownership.
Define backup/restore and schema migration approach for the chosen local service profile.
Define log/history retention separately from immutable artifact retention.

initialProfile.name: Windows Local Single-Host Integration Profile
initialProfile.python: Existing managed CPython 3.15.1 x64 interpreter; no global-Python fallback.
initialProfile.execution: Native local process execution; exact local Flow/Task runner and server/worker arrangement validated during implementation.
initialProfile.persistence: Local Prefect API/server with SQLite for first durable single-host profile; ephemeral loopback server only for non-durable tests.
conditions: If selected Prefect execution mode requires a server/worker, exact processes, ports, startup order, permissions and restart behavior must be documented.
Do not assume ephemeral PoC execution proves durable service behavior.

dependencyClasses.baseline: prefect==3.9.2 with full transitive lock and hashes
Local persistence for initial single-host profile
Only revisit for approved multi-worker/multi-server profile
Existing Draft 2020-12 schemas and managed Python jsonschema dependency

dependencyClosureDeliverables: Exact package lock and package hashes
Exact Python executable and environment verification
SQLite data location, restart, backup and migration evidence
Artifact store and Prefect result-storage separation

implementationPlan.name: Adoption Baseline and Contract Freeze
implementationPlan.objective: Turn the accepted Prefect decision and existing GPWCF/THIM contracts into a controlled implementation baseline.
work: Record this accepted decision in the project decision register without rewriting historical candidate evidence.
Inventory exact Stage/Step/SPU/Supporting Unit contracts and versions used by the first vertical slice.
Pin Prefect 3.9.2 and produce a reproducible dependency/license manifest under CPython 3.15.1.
Confirm the root invocation, Stage public facade, Step public execute and result contracts used by the reference consumer.
exitCriteria: No unresolved ownership contradiction between GPWCF, Prefect and Generator.
Exact runtime/package environment is reproducible on Windows x64.
No change to specialized contracts is made without a separately approved contract change.

implementationPlan.name: Prefect Native Capability Qualification
implementationPlan.objective: Prove the exact Prefect 3.9.2 constructs required by the target hierarchy in the selected local execution profile.
work: Build a minimal Root Flow invoking at least two Stage Parent Flows.
Build one Stage Parent Flow invoking at least two independently identifiable Step Subflows through public Step callables.
Bind at least two SPUs as Tasks inside their owning Step Subflows.
Exercise task dependency, fan-out/fan-in and repeated-child-flow concurrency under the exact selected runner/server profile.
Capture native run IDs, parent/child correlation, parameters, returns, exceptions and state transitions.
exitCriteria: Root, Stage, Step and executable-node boundaries are independently observable and correlated.
Step boundary is not bypassed.
Exact concurrency topology is understood and repeatable.
Unsupported native behavior is explicitly recorded.

implementationPlan.name: Functional Binding and Invocation Contract
implementationPlan.objective: Define the smallest explicit target-specific mapping between GPWCF callable contracts and Prefect definitions.
work: Define Functional Binding Manifest schema and versioning.
Define invocation/context envelope and identity correlation rules.
Define Stage Flow, Step Subflow, SPU Task and Supporting Unit binding declarations.
Define input/output serialization and artifact-reference handoff.
Define typed result, exception and Prefect-state mapping.
exitCriteria: All binding fields map to actual GPWCF specialized contracts.
No generic result/interface erases specialized semantics.
All native run IDs remain separate from GPWCF identities.

implementationPlan.name: Root and Stage Integration
implementationPlan.objective: Implement the Root Flow and all thirteen Stage Flow boundaries for the reference consumer, initially using fixture-backed Stage callables.
work: Implement root invocation and multiple Stage Flow inclusion/invocation.
Bind Stage facade inputs/outputs and Stage Flow Results.
Implement invocation-wide STG-01 and STG-02 reuse semantics.
Implement STG-02/STG-03 permitted overlap.
Implement exact Stage artifact-reference dependencies and conditional STG-13 admission.
exitCriteria: All 13 Stage boundaries are represented and independently correlated.
STG-01/STG-02 are not duplicated per payload type when environment scope is unchanged.
Stage dependency graph matches the Generator Pipeline contract.

implementationPlan.name: Step Subworkflow and SPU Functional Binding
implementationPlan.objective: Implement each concrete Step public callable as a nested Prefect Flow and bind its internal SPUs as native executable elements.
work: Derive actual GPWCF Step instances from Stage specialization and Step contracts; do not infer them from objective count.
Implement Step Subflow invocation through Step.execute.
Bind SPU callables and preserve SPUExecutionResult and StepExecutionResult independently.
Implement Step Composition flow result, returned results, invocation exceptions and Stage-facing aggregation.
Prove the Stage cannot bypass the Step boundary.
deliverables: SPU Task bindings and typed-result tests
exitCriteria: Each Step Subflow has distinct identity and public input/output/result contract.
Each SPU Task runs only within its owning Step composition boundary.
StepExecutionResult and SPUExecutionResult semantics are preserved.

implementationPlan.name: Supporting Unit Functional Binding
implementationPlan.objective: Bind only Supporting Unit patterns selected by concrete reference-consumer Steps and prove each applicable scope.
work: Inventory actual selected Validator, Observation and Error Handling units and their specialized contracts.
Implement executable Supporting Unit bindings at permitted scopes processingNode, stepSubworkflow, stageParentWorkflow and pipelineRoot only where the concrete contract authorizes them.
Keep Error Modeling as semantic definition/aggregation contract, not executable Task.
Implement specialized association binding only for contracts that require it.
Preserve observation event/activity and error-handler publication/custody semantics.
exitCriteria: Each selected unit's behavior/result/event/lifecycle semantics are preserved.
No generic Supporting Unit runtime type or mandatory association is introduced.
All required scope-validity and specialized association constraints pass.

implementationPlan.name: Artifact, Context, Result and Provenance Integration
implementationPlan.objective: Connect real Generator Stage artifacts through the Prefect hierarchy without changing their semantic ownership.
work: Implement artifact reference bridge and envelope verification.
Pass immutable IDs/digests/locations rather than large payloads through Prefect parameters/results.
Verify Stage 5/6 provider lineage and Stage 7 reconciliation inputs.
Verify Stage 10 context-bound PLD and Stage 11 representation-qualified SAM identities.
Verify Stage 12 exact validation-combination and Stage 13 manifest/package provenance.
exitCriteria: Every downstream artifact resolves to exact producer, input fingerprints and schema/version.
No in-place artifact mutation or identity-domain conflation.
Prefect state does not substitute for domain results.

implementationPlan.name: Lifecycle, Failure, Retry and Recovery
implementationPlan.objective: Prove operational settlement against GPWCF lifecycle and custody contracts.
work: Test cancellation propagation and actual process termination for native tools.
Test timeout settlement, including uncertain child process state.
Define retry/idempotency per safe operation and prohibit unsafe publication replay.
Test independent branch failure isolation and root aggregation.
Test Prefect server/worker restart and resumption/reconciliation for persisted runs.
Verify Step reuse/retirement and Supporting Unit quiescence/release outcomes.
exitCriteria: No cancelled/timed-out operation is assumed terminated without evidence.
Unresolved settlement preserves recovery ownership and access.
Retries cannot duplicate accepted side effects.
All required lifecycle states map to confirmed/failed/indeterminate GPWCF outcomes.

implementationPlan.name: Full Reference Consumer Acceptance and Release
implementationPlan.objective: Run the actual PayloadDescriptionGenerator through the adopted Prefect integration and close target acceptance gates.
work: Execute complete Stage 1-13 end-to-end runs using real stage implementations and fixtures.
Exercise multiple contexts, provider fan-out, representation profiles, validation outcomes and publication gating.
Run schema, artifact digest, deterministic serialization and package immutability checks.
Run Windows restart/recovery and resource-boundary tests.
Produce final conformance report and dependency manifest.
exitCriteria: All mandatory acceptance criteria pass or have explicitly approved scoped waivers.
No unresolved critical lifecycle, custody, result, identity or stage-boundary gap.
Prefect adoption is integrated-and-verified for the declared reference-consumer scope.

acceptancePlan.acceptancePolicy: Acceptance is evidence-based. Each test records Prefect version, Python executable/version, host OS/architecture, execution profile, test fixture/input digests, GPWCF identities, Prefect run IDs, outputs/artifact digests, logs, and pass/fail/blocked status. No test is marked passed from source inspection alone when runtime behavior is required.

architectureAcceptance.requirement: A Root Flow invokes at least two distinct Stage Parent Flows in one root execution.
architectureAcceptance.evidence: Root Flow run plus two independently identifiable Stage Flow runs and correlated GPWCF identities.

architectureAcceptance.requirement: A Stage Parent Flow invokes at least two Step Subflows through their public Step.execute contracts.
architectureAcceptance.evidence: Parent/child run trace, Step invocation envelopes and returned StepExecutionResults.

architectureAcceptance.requirement: Each Step Subflow contains its own bound SPU executable Tasks; Stage cannot invoke those Tasks directly.
architectureAcceptance.evidence: Binding manifest, call graph/trace and negative boundary test.

architectureAcceptance.requirement: Functional Binding covers all executable roles required by the reference consumer and each binding preserves its specialized contract.
architectureAcceptance.evidence: Complete binding manifest and contract conformance report.

architectureAcceptance.requirement: Supporting Units bind at each actually applicable permitted scope, without converting Error Modeling into an executable unit.
architectureAcceptance.evidence: Scope-specific positive/negative tests and pattern-specific contract traces.

architectureAcceptance.requirement: Association is used only for specialized contract semantics that require it; no Root Association is required by default.
architectureAcceptance.evidence: Relationship-to-native-mechanism mapping and negative test for unnecessary root association.

architectureAcceptance.requirement: GPWCF identity, typed result, exception, artifact and lifecycle evidence remain distinct from Prefect native execution metadata.
architectureAcceptance.evidence: End-to-end correlation report and schema validation.

stageAcceptance.verification: Execute at least two payload branches under one root; verify one STG-01 producer identity and exact inventory digest in both branches.

stageAcceptance.verification: Positive exact-digest case and negative changed-inventory case.

stageAcceptance.requirement: Per-TU effective invocations, compiler/frontend, language/target/ABI, headers/macros and context grouping retain provenance and unknown/conflict states.

stageAcceptance.requirement: AST observation package and diagnostics are independently identified and immutable.

crossCuttingAcceptance.name: Windows/Python Reproducibility
crossCuttingAcceptance.requirement: Fresh isolated environment reproduces Prefect 3.9.2 under managed CPython 3.15.1 x64 with no global fallback.

crossCuttingAcceptance.name: Hierarchy and Functional Binding
crossCuttingAcceptance.requirement: Root, Stage, Step, SPU and all selected Supporting Unit boundaries pass their respective binding/nesting contracts.

crossCuttingAcceptance.name: Typed Result and Exception Separation
crossCuttingAcceptance.requirement: SPUExecutionResult, StepExecutionResult, Stage Flow Result, domain errors and thrown exceptions remain separate from Prefect states.

crossCuttingAcceptance.name: Artifact Integrity and Custody
crossCuttingAcceptance.requirement: All artifact references resolve and preserve exact schema/version/digest/producer/input lineage; no large payload dependence on Prefect parameter/result storage.

crossCuttingAcceptance.name: Cancellation and Process Settlement
crossCuttingAcceptance.requirement: Cancellation/timeout is propagated and actual child-process termination and unresolved recovery custody are evidenced.

crossCuttingAcceptance.name: Retry and Replay Safety
crossCuttingAcceptance.requirement: Every enabled retry has explicit idempotency/reconciliation proof; no duplicate accepted publication or output.

crossCuttingAcceptance.name: Failure Isolation and Recovery
crossCuttingAcceptance.requirement: Independent branches, Stage failures, worker/service restarts and uncertain outcomes preserve recovery responsibility and immutable evidence.

crossCuttingAcceptance.name: Durable Local Execution
crossCuttingAcceptance.requirement: Local Prefect server/SQLite profile survives controlled restart and retains operational history independently of consumer artifacts.

crossCuttingAcceptance.name: Deterministic End-to-End Reference Run
crossCuttingAcceptance.requirement: Same pinned inputs/resources produce semantically identical outputs and exact immutable artifact references except declared run/time metadata.

buildAdoptAdapt.decision: This document resolves the previously open external workflow runtime selection in favor of Prefect.

openDecisions.question: Which exact Prefect task runner and native local execution mode should be the supported baseline for Stage/Step nesting and dynamic provider fan-out?
openDecisions.rule: Select from measured behavior in Prefect 3.9.2 on Windows/CPython 3.15.1; do not infer from fixture PoC topology.

openDecisions.question: What exact local API/server/worker arrangement is used for durable runs and what are its restart, persistence and recovery guarantees?
openDecisions.rule: Keep ephemeral test mode separate from durable local mode.

openDecisions.question: What are the concrete Stage/Step public callable types and actual GPWCF Step instances for each reference-consumer Stage?
openDecisions.rule: Derive from approved specialized contracts; Stage Model objectives/execution_steps are not a substitute.

openDecisions.question: Which Supporting Unit patterns and scopes are actually selected by each concrete Step/Stage/root?
openDecisions.rule: No pattern or scope is mandatory merely because it is available in framework model.

openDecisions.question: What artifact storage adapter and reference URI/path scheme are authoritative for each Stage artifact?
openDecisions.rule: Preserve existing consumer artifact contracts; do not move semantic ownership into Prefect storage.

openDecisions.question: What cancellation, timeout, process-tree termination and recovery guarantees can be implemented in selected local Prefect mode?
openDecisions.rule: Represent unsupported or indeterminate behavior explicitly; do not claim confirmed termination from orchestration state.

openDecisions.question: Which operations are safely retryable and what idempotency/reconciliation key is used for each?
openDecisions.rule: Default no retry for side-effecting operations until proven safe.

openDecisions.question: Which Stage 12 validation objectives/gates can execute concurrently without violating gate dependencies or deterministic aggregation?
openDecisions.rule: Preserve specified dependencies; parallelize only independently proven gates.

openDecisions.question: What are maximum inline parameter/result envelope sizes and artifact reference storage guarantees?
openDecisions.rule: Use small envelopes and immutable external artifact references; measure rather than guess.

conformanceStatus.targetHierarchicalIntegrationGate: documentary-design-defined; full Prefect conformance not yet proven
conformanceStatus.releaseRule: Do not mark HI-GATE-01, DEP-GATE-01..07, or full reference-consumer integration as passed until acceptance evidence is produced and reviewed.

changeControl.contractChangeRule: This architecture maps to existing GPWCF and Generator contracts. It does not authorize silent edits to specialized contracts, Stage specifications, schemas, artifact contracts or result semantics. Any required semantic change must be raised as an explicit change proposal, reviewed against its owning contract and approved before modification.
changeControl.evidenceRule: Record exact Prefect/Python versions, execution profile, test inputs, run IDs, GPWCF identities, artifacts, digests, logs and test outcomes for each acceptance run.
changeControl.repositoryRule: Preserve existing working-tree changes. Do not reset, checkout, clean, stage or commit as part of this architecture authoring task.
